units.spine: The Guild Council's standing at Spitzplatz is good enough to spend on decisions the town would otherwise refuse it.
The Guild Council's standing at Spitzplatz rests on the town's prosperity, and is worth exactly what that prosperity is worth and no more.
A stranger who comes to Spitzplatz to do business needs only one name and gets one answer, and can plan a season ahead on the strength of it.
There is trouble at Spitzplatz over the market levies, and nobody here needs it explained to them. Both sides now carry on as if the other has already lost.
The books of several houses at Spitzplatz are kept spotless, and that spotlessness is exactly what is being paid for.
There are interests at Spitzplatz that pull in different directions. None of them has hardened into a camp, and a question here is answered by whoever cares enough about it to answer.
Nobody in the town can put a single word on what kind of place it is governed as, not even the hall itself.

units.poolKey: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
units.spine: The town at Spitzplatz calls the hall by its full title in public and something shorter everywhere else, and both names are exact.
The Guild Council at Spitzplatz holds because it remains the heavier of the two, and the weighing is done again each season.

units.poolKey: legitimacyHold: public backing hardens the hold
units.spine: There are people at Spitzplatz who could move against the Guild Council and do not, because unseating a power the town stands behind costs more than the seat is worth.
